codeine.name: Codeine
codeine.mechanism: Ultrarapid CYP2D6 metabolizers convert codeine into morphine far faster than normal, pushing morphine to toxic levels even at a standard dose and causing respiratory depression.
codeine.stat_label: estimated ultrarapid metabolizers in this region
codeine.real_case: FDA Boxed Warning (Feb 2013), issued after a review of pediatric deaths and serious adverse events following tonsillectomy/adenoidectomy.
codeine.static_explanation: Ultrarapid CYP2D6 metabolizers convert codeine into morphine far faster than normal. A standard pediatric dose can push morphine to toxic levels, causing respiratory depression. This is why codeine and tramadol now carry a boxed warning against use after tonsillectomy in children.

carbamazepine.name: Carbamazepine
carbamazepine.mechanism: Carriers of HLA-B*15:02 face a dramatically elevated risk of Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, severe skin reactions, when prescribed carbamazepine.
carbamazepine.stat_label: allele frequency in Han Chinese cohorts (Chung et al., 2004)
carbamazepine.real_case: Chung et al., Nature (2004) first linked the allele to SJS/TEN; a 2011 NEJM trial showed mandatory pre-prescription screening in Taiwan prevented cases.
carbamazepine.static_explanation: Carriers of HLA-B*15:02 face a dramatically elevated risk of Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — severe, life-threatening skin reactions — when prescribed carbamazepine. The allele is common in this population and nearly absent in European populations.

abacavir.name: Abacavir
abacavir.mechanism: Carriers of HLA-B*57:01 can develop severe, sometimes fatal hypersensitivity reactions to this HIV medication.
abacavir.stat_label: carrier frequency (CPIC pooled data) vs 1-6.7% in most other regions
abacavir.real_case: PREDICT-1 trial, New England Journal of Medicine (2008) — prospective screening reduced confirmed hypersensitivity reactions from 2.7% to 0%.
abacavir.static_explanation: Carriers of HLA-B*57:01 can develop severe, sometimes fatal hypersensitivity reactions to this HIV medication. CPIC pooled data shows carrier rates in Southwest Asian populations well above most other regions studied, making pre-treatment screening especially consequential here.

clopidogrel.name: Clopidogrel
clopidogrel.mechanism: Poor CYP2C19 metabolizers can't efficiently activate this prodrug, so it fails to prevent clotting in stented patients, raising the risk of stent thrombosis and heart attack.
clopidogrel.stat_label: poor metabolizers documented in Vanuatu (Hsu et al., 2008)
clopidogrel.real_case: FDA Boxed Warning (2010) on reduced clopidogrel effectiveness in poor metabolizers.
clopidogrel.static_explanation: Poor CYP2C19 metabolizers can't efficiently activate this prodrug. In patients who've had a cardiac stent placed, that means the drug fails to prevent clotting — raising the risk of stent thrombosis and heart attack. Some Melanesian Pacific Island communities show among the highest poor-metabolizer rates ever documented, far above the ~3% typically seen in Caucasians.

warfarin.name: Warfarin
warfarin.mechanism: Two separate region-specific variants affect warfarin dosing: a VKORC1 variant lowering required dose in East Asians, and a distinct chromosome-10 variant in African-ancestry patients that standard dosing algorithms missed.
warfarin.stat_label: carry the dose-lowering VKORC1 variant in East Asian cohorts, vs ~39% in Europeans
warfarin.real_case: FDA warfarin label (2010) adds CYP2C9/VKORC1 dosing table; Perera et al., The Lancet (2013) identified the missing African-ancestry-specific variant.
warfarin.static_explanation: Two separate, region-specific variants affect warfarin dosing. A VKORC1 variant that lowers the required dose is far more common in East Asian populations than in Europeans. Separately, standard dosing algorithms — built mostly on European and Asian data — underpredicted doses for African-ancestry patients until a 2013 genome-wide study found a distinct chromosome-10 variant common in this population. Both cases show the same failure: a dosing table built on one population's genome missing another's.

isoniazid.name: Isoniazid
isoniazid.mechanism: Slow NAT2 acetylators break down this frontline tuberculosis drug more slowly, letting toxic intermediate metabolites build up in the liver.
isoniazid.stat_label: slow-acetylator genotype frequency in an Indian TB patient cohort (2024 study)
isoniazid.real_case: Indian pharmacogenetic studies (National Medical Journal of India, 2013; Monaldi Archives for Chest Disease, 2024) link slow-acetylator NAT2 genotype to anti-TB drug-induced liver injury.
isoniazid.static_explanation: Slow NAT2 acetylators break down this frontline tuberculosis drug more slowly, letting toxic intermediate metabolites build up in the liver. Indian studies find slow-acetylator status is both common and significantly associated with drug-induced liver injury in TB patients — a real concern given India's TB treatment burden.
